To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The number of isomers for alkanes up to C40 are tabulated and the average values of several graph theoretically defined invariants for these isomers are computed and tabulated; (2) The average value of several graph theoretical invariants are utilized in conjunction with a simple model to estimate several physical properties for these same isomers; (3) A brief survey of the literature is provided which indicates the utility of such data for a wide range of chemical problems.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of combinatorial enumeration methods for the enumeration of chemical isomers, and the extension of this methodology to the calculation of chemical properties of isomers.
chemical combinatorics, which we define as the application of combinatorics to chemistry.

a variety of combinatorial enumeration and averaging techniques that may be used to estimate the properties of large numbers of molecules, and to provide insight into the properties of individual molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work has demonstrated a new and general computational methodology, which can be utilized to compute a variety of structural and physicochemical properties for isomers of any chemical species of interest, and in particular, the alkane isomers.

we are able to provide a complete set of isomers of all types for up to N=40 carbons, and a complete set of structural isomers of all kinds up to N=80 carbons, with the latter set of isomers containing 1028 members, and with the former set containing 1014 members.
the present paper is a very good illustration of how chemical combinatorics can be used in the study of organic molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a methodology for the computation of the number of isomers and of several graph theoretically derived invariants averaged over structural isomers for a given number of carbons.
we can compute the average of any graph invariant (or other property) over all isomers of a given size, or for any isomer class, and we can do so in polynomial time.

we have shown how to extend standard combinatorial techniques to enable computation of isomer counts, isomer class averages of structural invariants, and estimates of physicochemical properties for structural isomers of alkanes and their derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard combinatorial enumeration of alkanes can be extended to a variety of chemically interesting invariants and thence to a variety of physicochemical properties.
a variety of structural invariants may be readily computed for isomers of alkanes and that the associated isomer count and average properties are of interest.

the chemical combinatorial enumeration of alkanes and their isomer classes is sufficiently tractable that the enumeration of the isomers and their properties can be computed to high accuracy and with reasonable efficiency.
